Chunking Strategies for Retrieval

Chunking splits a document into passages small enough to embed. The chunk boundary determines what a retriever can return, so a boundary drawn mid-argument costs recall that no reranker recovers.

Fixed-size windows

The simplest strategy slices on a character count with a fixed overlap. It is cheap and predictable, and it ignores document structure entirely.

Structural splitting

Splitting on headings respects the author's own boundaries. Sections that exceed the embedding budget are then split on length as a fallback.
